control_objective: Ensure all approved AI tool use cases are appropriately managed, monitored, and embedded into the core operational risk framework.
control_description: The Entity level ExCo (or equivalent) is responsible for ensuring that approved AI tool use cases are controlled in line with requirements set out in the Standard. The CISO and the Information Security Governance (ISG) team define documented processes, conduct periodic reviews of authorized use cases, and ensure all identified AI risks are formally factored into the Risk and Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) process.
control_evidence: Approved RCSA registers including AI-specific risks, ExCo meeting minutes endorsing AI use cases, and ISG periodic review documentation.
csa_checklist_item: Confirm that all approved AI tool use cases have been verified against standard requirements and formally factored into the entity's RCSA process.

control_name: Tiered AI Authorization and Change Board Review
control_objective: Prevent unauthorized deployment of business-impacting or standalone AI tools by enforcing a formalized change authorization workflow.
control_description: AI tool usage is split into Tier 1 (General Productivity) and Tier 2 (Business-Impacting Content). Any deployment of internet-based standalone AI tools or Tier 2 applications requires a formal 'AI Tool Use Case' request form backed by a business case signed off by a Department Head. The request must be submitted to the ISG team and routed to the AI Change Board for mandatory risk assessment, evaluation of technical/legal risks, and formal approval prior to implementation or deployment.
control_evidence: Completed 'AI Tool Use Case' request forms, ISG risk assessment reports, and AI Change Board approval logs.
csa_checklist_item: Confirm that any standalone or Tier 2 business-impacting AI use case has received formal approval from the AI Change Board via an authorized 'AI Tool Use Case' request form before deployment.

control_name: AI Data Protection and Encryption Standards
control_objective: Safeguard personal data, corporate trade secrets, and confidential information from unauthorized exposure through external AI platforms.
control_description: Utmost Group personnel are prohibited from entering personal data, confidential data, or corporate secrets (e.g., computer code and trade secrets) into prompts sent to an external standalone AI tool. To secure authorized integrations, handling of AI tool content must align with privacy requirements outlined in Utmost Entity Information Classification standards. Symmetric encryption must be utilized when the AI tool data is deemed confidential or secret, access controls must be enforced via Utmost Entity Access Control Standards, and information logging must conform to Utmost Entity Logging standards.
control_evidence: Technical architecture designs confirming symmetric encryption implementation, system-generated access control lists (ACLs), and AI platform interaction logs.
csa_checklist_item: Confirm that symmetric encryption, access controls, and logging protocols are actively enforced on all AI integrations handling confidential or secret data.

control_name: AI Content Verification and Misinformation Mitigation
control_objective: Mitigate risks associated with inaccurate, biased, or plagiarized AI-generated content before it impacts business operations or external stakeholders.
control_description: Authorised users of AI tools must critically assess and validate all AI-generated content before it is used or shared externally. This includes performing mandatory checks for potential biases, incomplete or factually inaccurate information, and intellectual property or copyright violations. Users are strictly prohibited from using AI to generate harmful, offensive, or discriminatory content, and must maintain administrative safety protocols such as turning off chat history or regularly deleting interactions to limit potential data breach exposure.
control_evidence: Documented evidence of content review in line with Appendix 4.2 (AI Tool Content Verification Approach), and user configuration logs verifying active data deletion practices.
csa_checklist_item: Confirm that all AI-generated content underwent formal bias, accuracy, and copyright validation prior to external publication or internal business reliance.

control_name: AI Tool Lifecycle and Triggered Risk Review
control_objective: Ensure ongoing compliance, validity, and security of authorized AI tools through scheduled and event-driven risk reviews.
control_description: Authorized AI tool use cases undergo periodic reviews by the ISG team at a frequency dependent on the risk level assigned during the authorization process. Additionally, immediate triggered reviews are initiated following significant changes to the organisation's structure, technology landscape, or regulatory environment, as well as following any security incidents or breaches related to AI tool usage to update relevant RCSA assessments.
control_evidence: Periodic review schedules, triggered risk assessment reports, stakeholder notifications, and updated RCSA outputs post-incident.
csa_checklist_item: Confirm that periodic reviews have been executed according to the assigned risk level, and that triggered reviews have been conducted for any significant technical changes or security incidents.

control_objective: Maintain a complete, audit-ready audit trail of all approved AI tool deployments and associated risk assessments.
control_description: The CISO and ISG team establish and maintain a central inventory of authorised AI tool use cases. Records of authorisation risk assessments, business case justifications, and periodic reviews must be retained for audit purposes. Technology Risk Assessments (TRAs) and Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs) which relate to AI tool usage will be retained outside of the core ISG team repository.
control_evidence: Copy of the Central AI Use Case Inventory, archived authorization records, and executed TRA/DPIA documentation.
csa_checklist_item: Confirm that the central inventory of authorized AI tool use cases is fully up to date and contains all required risk assessments and audit records.

control_name: Annual AI Risk Awareness and Training Program
control_objective: Ensure all personnel understand their responsibilities, the limitations of AI tools, and data protection requirements to prevent negligent risk exposure.
control_description: The ISG team is responsible for identifying and implementing appropriate AI tool awareness training processes. All Utmost Personnel who use AI tools must receive formal AI risk awareness training at a minimum on an annual basis. The training curriculum aligns with Appendix 4.1 objectives, ensuring users understand data minimisation, pseudonymisation techniques, fact-checking/verification methods, and reporting mechanisms for data protection issues.
control_evidence: Annual training curriculum materials aligned with Appendix 4.1 objectives, employee training completion logs, and compliance tracking reports.
csa_checklist_item: Confirm that 100% of personnel utilizing AI tools have completed the mandatory annual AI risk awareness training within the current cycle.

control_name: AI Content Labeling and Disclosure Framework
control_objective: Maintain clear transparency with internal and external stakeholders when AI tools are utilized to produce business-impacting content.
control_description: When AI tools are used to create Business-Impacting Content that could significantly influence user decisions or actions, full disclosure is required. For internal consumption, AI tool content must be clearly identified within the platform, remain version-controlled, and ensure user awareness of AI presence. For external consumption, public-facing content must be visibly labelled as AI-generated through watermarks, disclaimers, or prominent statements indicating its origin.
control_evidence: Samples of published internal and external materials containing standardized AI disclaimers, system metadata logs showing in-platform identification, and version control histories.
csa_checklist_item: Confirm that all generated 'Business-Impacting Content' contains the mandatory standard disclaimers and visible AI-origin watermarks/labels before distribution.

control_objective: Ensure all AI systems adhere to international regulatory mandates and avoid prohibited deployment configurations.
control_description: All AI use cases must align with the principles and requirements of the EU AI Act and related legislation. This includes enforcing risk classification requirements, avoiding prohibited use cases as defined by the regulation, implementing appropriate oversight for High-Risk AI systems, conducting DPIAs where applicable, and ensuring human oversight, transparency, and accountability are embedded in all AI deployments. Any planned development or integration must be reviewed and approved by the AI Change Board before implementation.
control_evidence: Regulatory mapping documents, formal risk classification records under the EU AI Act, sign-offs for High-Risk AI configurations, and completed DPIAs.
csa_checklist_item: Confirm that all planned AI developments and integrations have been reviewed against the EU AI Act risk classifications and approved by the AI Change Board prior to release.
